title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 115 (Resolutions requiring special notice)

content.overview: Section 115 supplies a special-notice procedure where the Act or a company's articles require special notice of a resolution.
content.glance: Eligible members give the company notice of their intention to move the resolution; the company then notifies members in the prescribed manner.
content.study:
## Scope and purpose

Section 115 applies when a provision of the Companies Act, 2013, or the company's articles requires special notice. It is a notice mechanism, not a standalone substantive ground for passing every resolution.

## Member notice and prescribed threshold

The intention to move the resolution must be notified to the company by members satisfying the prescribed threshold. Read section 115 with rule 23 of the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014, in its currently applicable form. Verify the threshold, service method and time limits against the current rule and facts.

## Company's notice to members

After receipt of a compliant special notice, the company must notify its members of the resolution in the manner prescribed by the Act and rules. This is distinct from the members' notice to the company. Keep evidence of receipt, dispatch and dates.

## Interaction with the substantive provision

For a proposed director removal, read section 115 with section 169 and its procedural safeguards, including the director's opportunity to be heard. Special notice alone does not mean that the resolution has passed.

## Checklist

Identify the provision requiring special notice; verify the members' eligibility and threshold; check timing and service; confirm that the company notified members; then apply the substantive resolution and meeting requirements.

sections.title: When required
content: Special notice applies where the Act or the articles require it.
Identify the substantive provision first; section 115 supplies the notice procedure.

sections.title: Two separate notices
content: Eligible members give notice of intention to the company under the prescribed rules.
The company then notifies members of the proposed resolution in the prescribed manner.

sections.title: Director removal
content: For removal of a director, apply section 169 and the relevant rules alongside section 115.
The special-notice procedure does not displace statutory safeguards or the director's opportunity to be heard.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: A properly incorporated company was challenged as indistinct from its controlling shareholder.
cases.issue: What is the legal effect of incorporation?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A registered company is a legal person separate from its members, even when control and ownership are concentrated.
cases.holding: The company's separate personality was affirmed.
cases.relevance: Use for Companies Act s. 9 and corporate personality.

cases.name: Foss v. Harbottle
cases.facts: Shareholders sought relief for alleged wrongs to the company.
cases.issue: Who may sue for a wrong done to the company and when may exceptions apply?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The company is the proper plaintiff for corporate wrongs, subject to recognised exceptions such as fraud on the minority and ultra vires acts.
cases.holding: The proper-plaintiff and majority-rule principles were established.
cases.relevance: Use with oppression, mismanagement and class-action analysis.

cases.name: Needle Industries (India) Ltd. v. Needle Industries Newey (India) Holding Ltd.
cases.facts: The Court examined share issue powers and alleged oppression.
cases.issue: When does a corporate action become oppressive or invalid?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The Court examines purpose, fairness, statutory power and resulting prejudice rather than treating every irregularity as oppression.
cases.holding: The corporate action was assessed under the statutory and equitable framework.
cases.relevance: Use for share allotment and oppression claims.

cases.name: Miheer H. Mafatlal v. Mafatlal Industries Ltd.
cases.facts: The Court reviewed a scheme of arrangement sanctioned by the company court.
cases.issue: What is the court's role in sanctioning a corporate scheme?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The court must ensure statutory compliance, class fairness, informed approval and absence of illegality, but does not substitute its commercial judgment for the company's decision.
cases.holding: The principles governing scheme sanction were stated.
cases.relevance: Use for corporate arrangements and tribunal scrutiny.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain special notice under section 115.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Section 115 applies when the Act or articles require special notice. Members meeting the prescribed threshold notify the company of their intention to move the resolution, and the company then notifies members in the prescribed manner. Read the provision with current rule 23 and the substantive provision requiring special notice; for director removal, section 169 safeguards also apply.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 115 (Resolutions requiring special notice). Where the Act requires special notice of a resolution, notice of the intention to move it is given to the company not earlier than three months and not less than fourteen days before the meeting. The section applies only to the persons, companies, and transactions it names. A filing, approval, or penalty arises only where the section or a rule under it says so. It does not create a power that is reserved to another section or to the Tribunal. Not a verified closure.
